modules.sourceReference: Day 1 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 7; answers cross-checked with facilitator page 10
modules.title: Day 1 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the definition of business analysis?
questions.explanation: Business analysis enables change by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value to stakeholders.

options.label: Enabling change by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value
Managing a project schedule, budget and delivery team
Writing software specifications without stakeholder involvement
Auditing completed projects for financial compliance

questions.question: How does the BA role differ from the Project Manager role?
questions.explanation: The BA defines the right solution; the Project Manager focuses on delivering the solution.

options.label: The BA defines the right solution; the PM delivers the solution
The BA owns the budget; the PM writes all requirements
The BA manages developers; the PM manages stakeholders
There is no practical difference between the two roles

questions.question: What are the six concepts of the BACCM™?
questions.explanation: The six core concepts are Change, Need, Solution, Stakeholder, Value and Context.

options.label: Change, Need, Solution, Stakeholder, Value and Context
Scope, Time, Cost, Quality, Risk and Resource
Plan, Build, Test, Release, Operate and Review
Vision, Mission, Goal, Strategy, Action and Result

questions.question: Name three of the six knowledge areas.
questions.explanation: The BABOK knowledge areas include Planning & Monitoring, Elicitation & Collaboration, Requirements Life Cycle Management, Strategy Analysis, Requirements Analysis & Design Definition and Solution Evaluation.

options.label: Strategy Analysis, Elicitation & Collaboration, and Solution Evaluation
Procurement, Cost Control, and Quality Assurance
Recruitment, Payroll, and Performance Management
Development, Deployment, and Infrastructure Operations

questions.question: What are the underlying competencies of a BA?
questions.explanation: The competency categories are Analytical Thinking, Behavioral Characteristics, Business Knowledge, Communication, Interaction and Software Knowledge.

options.label: Analytical, behavioral, business, communication, interaction and software knowledge
Budgeting, scheduling, procurement, auditing, hiring and contracting
Coding, testing, deployment, networking, security and support
Marketing, sales, advertising, branding, pricing and distribution

modules.sourceReference: Day 2 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 13; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 2 recap
modules.title: Day 2 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What are the three phases of Strategy Analysis?
questions.explanation: Strategy Analysis examines the current state, defines the future state and determines the change strategy needed to bridge the gap.

options.label: Analyze current state, define future state, and assess risks/change strategy
Elicit requirements, write code, and deploy software
Recruit staff, allocate desks, and approve payroll
Create a budget, run testing, and close the project

questions.question: What is a SMART objective?
questions.explanation: SMART objectives are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.

options.label: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound
Simple, Managed, Approved, Recorded and Tested
Strategic, Marketable, Agile, Repeatable and Technical
Scoped, Monitored, Assigned, Resourced and Traceable

questions.question: How do you identify stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Stakeholders are identified by considering everyone affected by, influencing, deciding on, funding or using the proposed change.

options.label: Identify people and groups affected by or able to influence the change
Include only the project sponsor and senior management
Include only people who will use the final system
Wait until requirements are complete before identifying anyone

questions.question: What is a RACI matrix?
questions.explanation: A RACI matrix clarifies who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for activities or decisions.

options.label: A responsibility chart showing Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed roles
A financial model for calculating return on investment
A diagram showing database entities and relationships
A method for ranking requirements by business value

questions.question: What are the four types of business risk?
questions.explanation: The module groups business risks as strategic, operational, financial and compliance risks.

options.label: Strategic, operational, financial and compliance
High, medium, low and closed
Internal, external, temporary and permanent
Scope, schedule, quality and communication

modules.sourceReference: Day 3 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 19; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 3 recap
modules.title: Day 3 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is elicitation?
questions.explanation: Elicitation is an iterative process of drawing out information from stakeholders and other sources.

options.label: An iterative process of drawing out information from stakeholders and other sources
A one-time meeting used to approve a finished specification
The technical process of converting requirements into code
A financial review performed after delivery

questions.question: Which set contains three valid elicitation techniques?
questions.explanation: Interviews, workshops and observation are established elicitation techniques; prototypes are another technique covered in the module.

options.label: Interviews, workshops and observation
Budgeting, procurement and auditing
Coding, deployment and monitoring
Recruitment, payroll and appraisal

questions.question: What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements?
questions.explanation: Functional requirements describe what a solution does; non-functional requirements describe how well it performs or the constraints it must meet.

options.label: Functional describes what the system does; non-functional describes how well it does it
Functional is mandatory; non-functional is always optional
Functional is technical; non-functional is purely financial
There is no difference between the two

questions.question: What does MoSCoW stand for?
questions.explanation: MoSCoW prioritises requirements as Must have, Should have, Could have and Won't have this time.

options.label: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time
Measure, Scope, Cost, Work and Output
Model, Specify, Confirm, Write and Operate
Mandatory, Standard, Conditional and Withdrawn

questions.question: Why is traceability important?
questions.explanation: Traceability links requirements to business goals, stakeholders and tests so coverage and the impact of change can be understood.

options.label: It links requirements to goals, stakeholders and tests and supports change impact analysis
It removes the need to validate requirements with stakeholders
It guarantees that a project will finish under budget
It replaces requirements prioritisation

modules.sourceReference: Day 4 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 26; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 4 recap
modules.title: Day 4 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What makes a good requirement?
questions.explanation: Good requirements are clear, complete, consistent, testable, feasible and traceable.

options.label: Clear, complete, consistent, testable, feasible and traceable
Short, technical, fixed, confidential and unreviewed
Ambitious, broad, informal and solution-specific
Approved only by the development team

questions.question: What is the difference between as-is and to-be models?
questions.explanation: An as-is model represents the current process or state; a to-be model represents the desired future process or state.

options.label: As-is shows the current state; to-be shows the desired future state
As-is shows requirements; to-be shows project costs
As-is is for users; to-be is only for developers
As-is is approved; to-be is rejected

questions.question: What is an ERD?
questions.explanation: An Entity Relationship Diagram models data entities and the relationships between them.

options.label: A diagram of data entities and their relationships
A register of project expenses and delivery dates
A chart of stakeholder influence and interest
A sequence of user-interface screens

questions.question: What is a user story format?
questions.explanation: The standard format is: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit].

options.label: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]
Given [budget], when [deadline], then [scope]
Who, what, when, where and cost
Problem, algorithm, code and test

questions.question: What is the difference between verification and validation?
questions.explanation: Verification checks requirement quality and correctness; validation checks that requirements and the solution meet stakeholder needs.

options.label: Verification checks quality; validation checks that the right needs are met
Verification is performed after delivery; validation is never required
Verification checks cost; validation checks schedule
They are identical quality activities

modules.sourceReference: Day 5 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 32; answers cross-checked with facilitator certification and competency guidance
modules.title: Day 5 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Solution Evaluation?
questions.explanation: Solution Evaluation assesses how well a deployed solution delivers value and identifies opportunities for improvement.

options.label: Assess value delivery and identify opportunities for improvement
Approve the original project budget before work begins
Replace stakeholder elicitation with system testing
Select the programming language for a solution

questions.question: Which factors indicate organizational readiness for change?
questions.explanation: Readiness is indicated by leadership support, stakeholder commitment, capability, capacity and effective communication and training plans.

options.label: Leadership support, stakeholder commitment, capability, capacity and change preparation
Only the availability of a technology budget
A completed solution with no user involvement
The number of requirements in the specification

questions.question: Which set contains three BA underlying competencies?
questions.explanation: Underlying competency categories include analytical thinking, communication, interaction, behavioural characteristics, business knowledge and software knowledge.

options.label: Analytical thinking, communication and interaction skills
Procurement, payroll and recruitment
Coding, deployment and network administration
Budget control, scheduling and contract management

questions.question: What are the three IIBA certification levels?
questions.explanation: The course identifies ECBA as entry-level, CCBA as intermediate and CBAP as advanced.

options.label: ECBA, CCBA and CBAP
CAPM, PMP and PRINCE2
PSM I, PSM II and CSM
Foundation, Practitioner and Architect

questions.question: How should you prepare for a BA certification exam?
questions.explanation: Effective preparation combines understanding the exam blueprint, studying BABOK concepts, practising questions and following a structured study plan.

options.label: Use the exam blueprint, study core concepts, practise questions and follow a study plan
Memorise terminology only on the day before the exam
Study software development tools instead of BA concepts
Skip practice questions to avoid learning incorrect patterns
